items.text: A bear bounced a ball beside a banana boat.
A bear bounced a ball beside a banana boat. A butterfly and a bird landed softly. “Best day ever!” hummed the bear.
A butterfly and a bird landed softly.
A cat baked a cake in a little car under a fluffy cloud.
A cat baked a cake in a little car under a fluffy cloud. Then it shared a cookie from a cup. Cozy and clever!
A dog and a duck met a gentle dinosaur.
A dog and a duck met a gentle dinosaur. They shared a donut, danced to a drum, and opened a bright door. Delightful day!
A duck said quack and found a quarter.
A flower bloomed as a firetruck zoomed by, and a fairy winked.
A fox and a frog watched a fish splash.
A fox and a frog watched a fish splash. A flower bloomed as a firetruck zoomed by, and a fairy winked. Fantastic fun!
A fox counted to six and began to mix.
A gift sat under a guitar while a goat munched nearby.
A giraffe in the garden plucked grapes.
A giraffe in the garden plucked grapes. A gift sat under a guitar while a goat munched nearby. “Gorgeous!” giggled the giraffe.
A heart of honey made everyone smile as a helicopter whirred past.
A horse wore a happy hat near a house.

A is for apple, round and sweet — a perfect after-playtime treat!
A is the very first letter — and one of the oldest letters ever written!
A jellyfish jiggled, jam tasted sweet, and a jet streaked across the sky.
A kangaroo flew a kite with a key on a string.
A kangaroo flew a kite with a key on a string. The king danced in the kitchen with a tiny kitten. Keep kicking, K!
A lion under a leaf licked a lemon lollipop by a lamp, then climbed a ladder of light.
A lion under a leaf licked a lemon lollipop by a lamp, then climbed a ladder of light. Lovely!
A lion's roar can be heard from 5 miles away!
A monkey and a mouse climbed a mountain under the moon, sipping milk and spotting a mushroom.
A monkey and a mouse climbed a mountain under the moon, sipping milk and spotting a mushroom. Magical!
A notebook held noodle doodles next to a net.
A penguin played piano while a pig ate pizza.
A penguin played piano while a pig ate pizza. A pencil drew a puppy. Perfect!
A rabbit rode a rocket over a rainbow.
A rabbit rode a rocket over a rainbow. A robot smelled a rose in the soft rain. Ready, set, roar!
A robot smelled a rose in the soft rain.

A turtle nibbled a tomato and found a shiny tooth.

A van carried a violin past a volcano full of vegetables. Someone wore a vest and pushed a vacuum. Vivacious!
A whale watched water through a window.
A whale watched water through a window. A worm checked a watch from a red wagon. Wonderful!
A worm checked a watch from a red wagon.

A yak bounced a yo-yo with yellow yarn on a yacht, then spooned yogurt. Yes, yes, yes!
A zebra zipped to the zoo.
A zebra zipped to the zoo. Zero worries — just a zigzag path past a zucchini patch. Zany and fun!

An airplane flew over an alligator, and an astronaut waved hello.
An ant found a shiny apple by an anchor.
An ant found a shiny apple by an anchor. An airplane flew over an alligator, and an astronaut waved hello. What an amazing A adventure!
An eagle soared above the earth, carrying an envelope to a friendly elf.
An elephant found a golden egg.
An elephant found a golden egg. An eagle soared above the earth, carrying an envelope to a friendly elf. Exciting!
An insect hummed while an iron pressed a flag, and an iguana lounged in the sun.
An octopus hugged an orange near a warm oven while an ostrich raced by.
An owl watched the ocean. An octopus hugged an orange near a warm oven while an ostrich raced by. Oh my!

An x-ray showed a xylophone in a box. A fox counted to six and began to mix. Extra exciting!
Apple. Apple. Apple. I see a red apple.
At night, a nose sniffed a nest.
At night, a nose sniffed a nest. A notebook held noodle doodles next to a net. Nice and neat!
B is for bear, so soft and round — the friendliest animal in town!
Birds build nests using twigs, grass, mud, and even soft feathers!
Blue whales are the largest animals that have ever lived on Earth!
C can sound like K (cat) or S (city) — a letter with two voices!
C is for cat, with whiskers neat — curling up on a sunny seat!
D is for dog, who loves to play — chasing balls all day!
Dogs can learn over 100 words — just like you are learning letters!
E is for elephant, big and gray — swinging its trunk every day!
E is the most-used letter in English books and stories!
Everyone shared a smile and a cozy sock.
F is for frog, who hops so high — from lily pad up to the sky!
Fish have been swimming in Earth's waters for over 500 million years!
G is for giraffe, so tall and kind — leaves of the trees are easy to find!
Giraffes are the tallest animals on Earth — their necks can be 6 feet long!
Great! Now find the big capital letters!
H is for horse, who loves to run — under the warm and golden sun!
Hi friend! I am your buddy voice.
Hi friend! I am your teacher voice.
I is for ice cream, cold and sweet — the yummiest summer treat!
Ice cream melted by an igloo on an island.
Ice cream melted by an igloo on an island. An insect hummed while an iron pressed a flag, and an iguana lounged in the sun. Incredible!
Igloos are made of snow bricks that keep the inside surprisingly warm!
J is for juice, so bright and sweet — orange, apple, a morning treat!
Jellyfish have been floating in the ocean for longer than dinosaurs lived!
Juice dripped on a jacket in the jungle.
Juice dripped on a jacket in the jungle. A jellyfish jiggled, jam tasted sweet, and a jet streaked across the sky. Joyful jump!
K is for kite, up in the blue — dancing and twirling just for you!
Kangaroos can hop faster than most people can run — over 30 miles an hour!
L is for lion, with a golden mane — the bravest roar on the plain!
Let's learn the alphabet! Tap any letter to begin.
M is for moon, so silver and bright — lighting up the quiet night!
N is for nest, high in a tree — a soft little home for a bird family!
No two zebras have the exact same stripe pattern — just like fingerprints!
O is for owl, so wise and deep — watching the forest while children sleep!
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood — super ocean superheroes!
P is for penguin, dressed in a suit — sliding on ice is its favorite route!
Penguins can't fly in the air — but they fly through water like rockets!
Q almost always brings its best friend U along — like in queen and quiet!
Q is for queen, with a sparkling crown — waving hello all over town!
R is for rocket, ready to go — 3, 2, 1… blast off, ho ho!
Rainbows appear when sunlight shines through raindrops at just the right angle!
S is for sun, so warm and bright — filling the morning with golden light!
Some trees live for thousands of years — older than castles and kings!
Someone wore a vest and pushed a vacuum.
T is for tiger, with stripes so bold — a story of courage retold!
The king danced in the kitchen with a tiny kitten.
The letter B started as a drawing of a house in ancient picture writing!
The Moon is about 238,000 miles from Earth — that's a very long hop!
The queen quilted quietly. “Question?” she asked. A duck said quack and found a quarter. Quite quirky!
The sun and a star smiled on a snake on a ship.
The sun and a star smiled on a snake on a ship. Everyone shared a smile and a cozy sock. Super!
The Sun is so big that a million Earths could fit inside it!
Then it shared a cookie from a cup.
They shared a donut, danced to a drum, and opened a bright door.
U is for umbrella, open and wide — keeping you dry when you play outside!
Under an umbrella, a unicorn put on a uniform, looked up, and strummed a ukulele.
Under an umbrella, a unicorn put on a uniform, looked up, and strummed a ukulele. Unbelievable!
Unicorns are mythical — but narwhals have a real spiral tusk that looks magical!
V is for violin, singing so sweet — making music with dancing feet!
Violins make music with four strings and a bow — tiny but mighty!
W is for whale, singing deep blue songs — the ocean is where a whale belongs!
X is for xylophone, ding ding ding — colorful bars that love to sing!
X says ks, like in box — and x-ray!
X-rays help doctors see bones inside your body — like magic vision!
Y is for yo-yo, spinning around — up and down without a sound!
Yaks live high in cold mountains and have super thick, warm fur!
Yes! Ice cream starts with I!
